history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN-ASSOCIATED PROTECTIVE-DEITY SHRINE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Bhomiyaji (Bhomiaji Maharaj) is the revered protector deity of Sammed Shikharji; jainsamaj.org describes him as world-famous alongside Rajasthan's Nakoda Bhairav, watching over pilgrims on the mountain day and night. At the Madhuban foothill there is a fascinating temple of Baba Bhomia housing his haloed idol, worshipped with oil and vermilion. Every year on Holi day a grand fair is held at the Baba's door. UNVERIFIED: the shrine's age, builder and architecture are not reliably documented. Coordinates are approximate (Madhuban foothill).

name: Bhomiyaji Sthan, Madhuban
town: Madhuban (CSV town 'Giridih' is WRONG - the shrine is at Madhuban village, Pirtand block)
town_description: Madhuban is the base village of Parasnath Hill in Pirtand block, Giridih district, Jharkhand. It is the gateway to Shri Sammed Shikharji Tirth, where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras are believed to have attained moksha. The village hosts popular Jain temples such as Samosharan and Bhomiyaji Asthan, and a Jain Museum whose balcony telescope gives a clear sight of the Parasnath temple. Trekking routes of 9-13 km to the hilltop start here; Parasnath railway station is about 25 km away.
tradition: Jainism (protective folk deity of the Shikharji pilgrimage)
